$comment: PINNED SCREEN PARAMETERS. Written before the screen was run against any stranger wallet, and
committed in their own commit so the ordering is the audit trail. Every number is anchored to a
measurement that already exists in this repository or in a committed scout report, and the
anchor is named in `justification`. Do not move a value to fit an output. If a value must
change, change it here, say why in the PR, and re-run Stage 0 first: a screen that no longer
reproduces the answers we already know is not ready to judge strangers.
SCOPE: this tool GATES on competence and SCORES ENTRY. It does not recommend, and it does not
score EXIT — see `stage2_entry`.
Keyed, MadeOnSol, one request per candidate. A GATE, not a score: it asks whether a
deployer is competent, which is necessary and nowhere near sufficient. Stage 0 demonstrates
the gap empirically — it shows the gate PASSING the one deployer we know is not worth the
time.
The denominator is `profile.pump_tokens[].complete` and nothing else. Never `bonding_rate`,
`total_bonded`, `total_tokens_deployed`, `recent_bond_rate`, `recent_outcomes` or
`best_token_peak_mc`, which are trailing windows or stale; and never
/deployer-hunter/{wallet}/tokens, which is bonded-only and so has no denominator at all.

justification.minTokens: MadeOnSol's own spec tells consumers to gate on labeled_tokens >= 3. That is far too low: on our subject deployer a 22-token window read 0.6818 against a true 0.4310, so a window of ~22 was enough to be wrong by 58% relative. 25 is the floor at which their sliding-window artefact stops being the whole measurement, and it is 8x their published gate. It is NOT enough for a lifetime claim, which is why the span is reported alongside and why long-horizon consistency is reported UNMEASURED.
justification.minCompletionRate: 0.25 is MadeOnSol's own published 'good' tier lifetime bar. Our subject deployer's true lifetime rate is 0.4310 (239 launches, 103 bonded) and it is a genuinely competent operator, so a bar meaningfully below that admits the population we care about while excluding deployers that mostly fail.
justification.minSpanDays: A high rate earned inside a single day is a burst, not a record. 14 days is the shortest span over which pump.fun's own time-to-bond distribution puts a large majority of eventual graduations behind us: on our tape 82.5% of graduations occur within 7 days and 85.4% within 14.

$comment: The captain's word was 'consistently'. MadeOnSol cannot answer it: their only
denominator-complete surface (profile.pump_tokens) is capped at 70 records and about 35 days.
Manufacturing a long-horizon claim from a 35-day window is exactly the defect we found in
their own aggregate, so the tool does not do it. Long-horizon consistency is reported as
UNMEASURED unless --consistency is passed, which pages a keyless pump.fun creator listing and
spends no quota.

justification.epochDays: 30-day epochs are long enough that an epoch is not one week of luck, and short enough that a 6-month history yields the 3 required.
justification.maxDispersion: max(epoch rate) - min(epoch rate) > 0.35 FLAGS a deployer as streaky rather than excluding it. A flag, not a filter: the point of the exercise is that one hot window must not read as a record, and the reader is entitled to see the spread rather than have it silently applied.

$comment: Bounds for the creation-derived launch history — the walk that answers 'which tokens did this
wallet CREATE' instead of 'which tokens does it OWN NOW'. See creation.mjs for why the two
differ and for the on-chain observation that established it.
This walk is the expensive part of a run by an order of magnitude, because the only keyless
index that reaches a create transaction is the wallet's own signature index, and for a pump.fun
deployer that index is dominated by strangers' failed trades. Every bound here is therefore a
hard ceiling, and readCreatedHistory reports which one bit rather than truncating silently.
The walk covers a CONTIGUOUS WINDOW BACKWARDS FROM NOW. Inside it every creation is found;
outside it none is, and mergeHistories falls back to the ownership listing and says so. A
create count read as a lifetime figure under any stopReason other than 'index-exhausted' is
wrong in the same direction as the vendor's sliding 'lifetime' window.

justification.maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate: Measured 2026-08-02: sustained keyless throughput against api.mainnet-beta is about 0.42 transactions/second, i.e. roughly one request per 2.4s including backoff, and a create is found by inspecting every SUCCEEDED signature in the wallet's index. The success fraction varies enormously between deployers — 1.7% on the busiest wallet screened, 99.7% on another — so the cost of a full history ranged from 7 minutes to 84 hours across the 12 wallets of runs/2026-07-29-elite.json. 100 requests is a per-candidate ceiling that keeps a 12-candidate run inside about 50 minutes; on a quiet wallet it is the whole history, on a busy one it is a window of hours and the record says so. NOTE THE OTHER END OF THAT ARITHMETIC: at the 195-candidate cap it is 19,500 requests and ~13.5 HOURS, which is the dominant cost of a default run — --candidates N is the lever that bounds it, and --ownership-only skips it for a fast pass whose bias is stamped into the record. See CREATION-DERIVED.md for the per-wallet costs.
justification.maxSignaturePages: 200 pages is 200,000 signatures, past which no keyless walk is finishing inside a session. It exists so a wallet with an enormous index cannot turn the request ceiling into the only brake.
justification.txBatchSize: 1, and the 1 is measured. report.md 9.4 recorded batches of 5-8 getTransaction as sustainable, and that no longer holds: on 2026-08-02, fetching the same transactions at batch=1 took 58s with ZERO load-shed events, batch=4 took 76s with 7, and batch=8 took 110s with 11. Throughput was 0.42 tx/s at batch=1 and 0.36 tx/s at batch=8 — the endpoint weights each entry of a JSON-RPC batch against its limiter, so a batch of 8 spends 8 tokens and buys nothing but backoff. Batching is therefore actively harmful HERE TOO, exactly as it is on pump.fun's keyless endpoints. The client still supports batching, capped at 8, because the endpoint's behaviour is the vendor's to change and re-measuring is cheaper than rebuilding.
justification.rpcMinIntervalMs: 1,400ms is the documented floor, but a 200-request run at that pace on 2026-08-02 took over 890 seconds instead of the expected 280 — the endpoint was shedding load and the retry backoff was paying for it. 2,500ms is the observed rate at which that stops happening, so it is faster in wall-clock than the nominally quicker setting. api.mainnet-beta rate-limits GLOBALLY across getSignaturesForAddress and getTransaction, and two concurrent jobs earned a sustained 429 lockout, so this is one queue with one request in flight.

$comment: Hard bounds, enforced in code. There is no flag that disables one.
CAPTAIN'S INSTRUCTION, 2026-08-02: 'There is no current free method to save on the madeonsol
key request limits ... use all free tier daily quota as needed if it gets results.' These
bounds are therefore the FULL Free-tier daily allowance (~200 requests/day), not a fraction
of it. An earlier quarter-allowance ceiling of 45 was this tool's own caution, never a
captain instruction, and it is WITHDRAWN — do not reintroduce it or re-derive it: there is no
free substitute for this data, so an unspent allowance buys nothing and only leaves questions
unanswered.
The conditional binds: 'if it gets results'. This authorises sizing a run by what the
question needs. It does NOT authorise sweeping, idle retrying, or re-running to re-evidence a
side observation. A run that cannot say in advance what it will answer does not get the
allowance.
SCOPE: this relaxation is MadeOnSol ONLY. The Helius / SolanaTracker / CoinGecko keys are
shared with production and the standing 'do not waste the quota that is production quota too'
is unchanged, as is the keyless pump.fun pacing below, which bounds a shared public resource
for an entirely different reason.
The burst limit is NOT relaxed either: ~10/minute is a rate the vendor enforces, not a
self-imposed caution, so keyedMinIntervalMs stays.

justification.maxKeyedRequests: 200 is the whole Free-tier daily allowance as measured (see tools/deployer-screen/README.md). Enumeration costs 3 (recent-bonds, alerts, leaderboard) and the gate costs 1 per candidate, so the 195-candidate cap costs 198 worst case and the remaining 2 are the retry headroom. A run whose PLANNED worst case exceeds this is refused before its first request rather than allowed to die part-way through. STAGE 2 ADDS NOTHING TO THIS: it reuses the profile Stage 1 already fetched and spends no keyed request of its own.
justification.maxCandidates: 195 = 200 - 3 enumeration - 2 retry headroom, i.e. the cap is whatever the allowance leaves rather than a judgement about how many deployers are worth grading. It is also well above what the three enumeration queries can surface (50 + 100 + 50 rows, heavily overlapping and then pre-filtered), so the DEFAULT run grades everything it surfaces and coverage truncation becomes the exception it is supposed to be.
justification.keyedMinIntervalMs: Free tier bursts at ~10/minute. 6.5s between request starts keeps a run under that with margin, and margin matters because the allowance is shared. This is the vendor's rate limit, not our caution, so raising the daily bounds does not touch it. A full 198-request run therefore takes about 21 minutes, which is the intended cost of respecting the burst limit — but THAT IS NO LONGER THE RUN'S WALL CLOCK AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. The default history source is creation-derived, and the Solana RPC walk dominates everything else by an order of magnitude: 195 candidates x 100 requests x 2.5s is ~13.5 HOURS on its own. Add ~21 minutes keyed, ~26 for the gate's ownership listing on frontend-api-v3, ~50 for Stage 2 on swap-api, and a further ~19.5 with --consistency, and a full default run at the candidate cap is ABOUT 15 HOURS end to end, or ~15.5 with --consistency. An earlier version of this note said 47 minutes; it predated the creation walk and was wrong by a factor of twenty. DO NOT KILL A DEFAULT RUN FOR STILL GOING AFTER AN HOUR. The liveness signal is not the same on every leg: the keyed and frontend-api-v3 clients print one line per request, but the creation walk would emit ~20,000 of those, so it prints a PERIODIC HEARTBEAT — the first request of each candidate and then every tenth, i.e. a line roughly every 25 seconds at this walk's 2.5s pacing, showing that candidate's spend against maxRpcRequestsPerCandidate. Watch that counter rather than expecting a line per request, and use --candidates N to bound the run (the RPC leg is N x 100 x 2.5s) or --ownership-only to skip the walk entirely for a fast pass whose bias towards rejection is stamped into the record. renderDryRun prints this arithmetic for whatever flags are actually passed.
justification.keylessMinIntervalMs: GOVERNS ONE HOST: frontend-api-v3.pump.fun — the gate's ownership listing and the --consistency creator walk, which share one client. It does NOT govern the Stage 2 fill walk, which has its own pinned pacing (`stage2_entry.keylessMinIntervalMs`) because it reaches a different host that behaves differently. THIS VALUE IS A CONSERVATIVE CARRY-OVER, NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE ENDPOINT IT GOVERNS, and the correction matters: the ~0.5 requests/second figure this was originally justified by was measured against api.mainnet-beta.solana.com, and the June report's own spend table records BOTH swap-api.pump.fun and frontend-api-v3.pump.fun as NOT CONTACTED — so it was never a pump.fun measurement at all. It is kept because it is conservative and because frontend-api-v3 has shed nothing in this tool's use of it; if that host is ever measured, this number should be re-derived from that measurement rather than from a different host's. Either way it bounds a shared public resource rather than expressing our own caution, so the MadeOnSol relaxation does not touch it. The RETRY COUNT is a separate question and is not this bound: a keyless request is retried on a 429 or a 5xx, and each attempt counts against maxKeylessRequests.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: A PER-CLIENT CEILING, NOT A RUN TOTAL, and the distinction is what the code enforces: screen.mjs builds TWO independent keyless clients, and this value bounds only the general one (frontend-api-v3). Stage 2 runs on its own client under its own `stage2_entry.maxKeylessRequests` of 432, which this number neither contains nor constrains, so the enforced combined worst case is 1,400 + 432 = 1,832 requests. 1,400 is sized to COVER the candidate cap rather than to bound it, and it is sized for what the code now actually spends on this client, which is TWO passes and not one. The GATE reads the ownership listing it merges the creation window with, up to 4 pages PER CANDIDATE (screen.mjs LISTING_PAGES_FOR_MERGE); the --consistency pass then costs up to 3 pages per gate SURVIVOR, and every candidate can be one. So 195 candidates cost 195 x 4 = 780 for the gate plus 195 x 3 = 585 for consistency = 1,365 worst case, and the remaining 35 are the retry headroom. The earlier 600 was justified on the consistency pass alone and was already exceeded by gating at the default candidate cap. A keyless ceiling below the plan would make the tool stop looking part-way through a run it had already paid for in KEYED quota, and an unmeasured candidate is not a measured one — so screen.mjs now also REFUSES a plan whose keyless worst case does not fit, before its first request, exactly as it does for the keyed one. Raising the count does not lean harder on pump.fun — keylessMinIntervalMs is unchanged, so what it buys is wall-clock time and nothing else: 1,365 requests at 2s is ~45.5 minutes, of which ~26 is the gate's own 780 pages. That is a minority of the run's wall clock rather than the whole of it — see keyedMinIntervalMs, where the creation walk's ~13.5 hours puts a full default run at ABOUT 15 HOURS. The June report sustained 460 consecutive keyless requests at 1.4s apart with zero shedding. These are pump.fun's free endpoints — no key, no vendor allowance, and no shared quota is touched by any of it.

$comment: ACTIVE. This is the `stage2_seam` block of thresholds v2.0.0, promoted in place — the two
values it reserved were pinned by the stage-0/1 lane BEFORE this lane existed to apply them,
and they are carried over unchanged with their original justification. That ordering is the
audit trail and it is the reason the block was not rewritten: a bar derived after seeing the
output it judges is not a bar. See git history for the superseded block verbatim.
What Stage 2 answers, from the captain's brief verbatim: 'Can I beat the dev and all other
wallets sniping the same tokens created by the dev currently?' — the ENTRY half of it.
(1) ENTRY ROOM: how much of the opening window the dev and its own cohort take before an
outsider is filled. The method of slot-zero-june-regime-change/report.md 5.1, 'the
operation's share of the curve's bottom'. In the captain's own framing, which is the
one the docs keep: this measures HOW BADLY CONFIGURED THE DEV'S OWN LAUNCH BOT IS.
(2) THE FIELD: what every OTHER sniping wallet on those same tokens achieved — fill, queue
position, and realised P&L. The question is whether WE beat them, so the competition is
measured and never assumed.
Both are keyless, from pump.fun fills. Stage 2 spends NO keyed request: it reuses the mint
list from the profile Stage 1 already fetched.
REPORTED AS DISTRIBUTIONS PLUS A HIT RATE, NEVER A MEAN. A standing captain bar for this
class of claim. Sniper outcomes are heavy-tailed on both sides, so a mean describes nobody.
NOT SCORED HERE, AND NO EXIT SIGNAL MAY REACH AN ENTRY NUMBER: exit feasibility (when the dev
sells relative to mint and to outsider inflow, whether the trigger is a SIZE and therefore
caps our position because our own buy counts towards it, and whether an outsider could have
exited first) is stage 3's separate deliverable. The prediction-grading loop is another lane
again. Room to enter is not room to leave, and one blended number cannot be read back apart.

justification.minRoomLeft: CARRIED UNCHANGED from thresholds v2.0.0 `stage2_seam.reservedMinRoomLeft`, pinned before this lane existed. Anchored on the only regime this project has MEASURED as profitable for create-slot outsiders. June report 5.1 puts the operation's share of the curve's bottom at 0.451 before 2026-06-04 (room 0.549) and 0.768 after (room 0.232); 6.1 puts create-slot outsiders at +6.54 then +1.79 SOL per launch, and later entrants at +5.43 then -0.74. So room >= 0.55 is the pre-step regime and nothing tighter has ever been observed to pay.
justification.minLaunchesSampled: CARRIED UNCHANGED from `stage2_seam.reservedMinLaunchesSampled`. A distribution over fewer launches is not a distribution, and the June report's own per-launch cuts are the reason: its era-B bucket of 22 launches was the smallest it was willing to state a quartile spread over.
justification.minFieldRoundTrips: A hit rate is the headline number of the field leg, and one over a handful of round trips is noise wearing a percentage sign. 10 is the floor at which a single outcome cannot move the rate by more than 10 points. Below it the field is reported UNMEASURED rather than estimated.
justification.minFieldHitRateGross: A NECESSARY CONDITION, NEVER A SUFFICIENT ONE, and it can only ever take a verdict away. The fill tape is gross of fees, so this rate is an upper bound: on our own subject's post-2026-06-04 launches it reads 0.765 while the fee-inclusive record puts the whole outsider population at +0.54 SOL per launch with 51 of 106 wallets negative. Below 0.5 the field loses money before costs and therefore certainly after them, which is conclusive; above it, nothing whatsoever is established. Stage 0 asserts that this leg cannot carry a positive verdict on its own.
justification.maxCandidatesScored: Stage 2 is the expensive leg per candidate — up to 144 keyless requests and about 17 minutes at the pinned 7s pacing — while Stage 1 costs one request per candidate. Scoring 3 of the gate's survivors bounds a full run at about 50 minutes worst case, and a typical one at about 17 minutes at the measured p50 of 4 pages; the committed elite run passed 5 of 12, so 3 is a real cap and the run reports how many survivors it dropped.
justification.maxLaunchesPerCandidate: Equal to minLaunchesSampled, so a candidate is either scored on a full sample or reported UNMEASURED. Sampling more would not sharpen the distribution enough to justify a proportional increase in the request bound, and sampling fewer could never clear the floor.
justification.maxRequestsPerLaunch: MEASURED from the committed tape's own build metadata across 235 launches, and it corrects a first pass that sampled one file and got this wrong. Pages needed per launch: p50 4, p90 8, p95 13, MAX 24. The cap is on REQUESTS rather than pages because the endpoint sheds ~24.7% of what it is asked for (51,715 OK against 16,960 HTTP 429 on that same build) and the client retries; counting only successes would let a launch cost 3x the printed plan. 18 requests is about 13-14 successful pages at the measured shed rate, so it covers roughly the 95th percentile launch. THE BOUND IS EXACT RATHER THAN APPROXIMATE: a page can cost up to 3 requests (one attempt plus two backoffs), so the walk reserves the WHOLE per-page cost before starting a page and a launch therefore costs at most 18 and never 20. Checking the cap only between pages would have let a walk with one request of headroom spend three, breaking the stage arithmetic the dry run prints as the entire exposure. THE TAIL IS DROPPED, NOT TRUNCATED SILENTLY: a launch that spends the cap without reaching the mint is reported as DROPPED with its own note, and the sampling bias is stated because the launches too busy to walk are exactly the interesting ones.
justification.keylessMinIntervalMs: GOVERNS ONE HOST: swap-api.pump.fun, the fill walk, and only it. `budget.keylessMinIntervalMs` stays at 2000ms for frontend-api-v3, which has shed nothing here and must not be slowed for a fault on a different host. 7000ms is anchored on TWO INDEPENDENT READINGS OF THIS HOST. (i) LIVE: at 2000ms two consecutive Stage 2 runs against swap-api each lost 4 of the subject's 8 launches to HTTP 429 after all three attempts, so the run reported `entry-unmeasured` where the truth is `entry-room-absent`; the same code at 7000ms walked all 8 and produced `entry-room-absent`. A fast wrong answer is worth nothing, and the failure is silent in the direction that matters — a dropped launch degrades the verdict rather than announcing the pacing is wrong. (ii) THE TAPE BUILDER'S OWN RECORD against this same endpoint: the committed `window/*.meta.json` `delay` field — the adaptive delay each build settled on — reads p50 4.92s, p75 15s, p90 15.5s, max 40s, with only p10-p25 near 1.2s; and its shed share is ~24-25% FLAT across every delay bucket, so backing off does not buy immunity and there is no cheap corner to sit in. 7s is therefore pinned deliberately between that p50 and p75 rather than at the bottom of the range. COST: the request arithmetic is untouched — 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 still — but the wall clock is not, so the typical run is about 17 minutes and the worst case about 50, and every printed estimate says so.
justification.keylessRetryBackoffMs: The tape build shed a quarter of its requests and its own recorded delay ranges from 0.75s to 40s, i.e. it backed off and retried through them. A client that treats a 429 as terminal cannot walk this endpoint at all - the first live check of the pager died on one, three launches in. Two retries at 3s and 9s clear the ordinary case, and EVERY attempt counts against both the per-launch cap and the stage ceiling, so a retry-heavy run gets a dropped launch rather than an unbounded one.
justification.tradePageLimit: 100 is what the trade endpoint serves per page and is the figure the AGENTS.md note is anchored on. Asking for less would multiply the request count for no benefit; the endpoint's own cap is what it is.
justification.windowMs: 60000 is the committed population tape's own window_ms. It is used for TWO things only: deciding a launch is old enough to have finished happening, and placing the seek cursor. It does NOT decide which fills are inside the measured window — windowSlotSpan does — because the mint time it would be measured from comes from the vendor and the fills come from pump.fun, and there is nothing to reconcile the two clocks with.
justification.windowSlotSpan: MEASURED, and deliberately NOT ceil(windowMs/400)=150, which is measurably too narrow. Across the 210 committed launches whose stored window_ms is 60000 the observed slot span is p50 151, p75 153, p90 155, p95 155, MAX 158 — and 51% of them hold at least one fill beyond createSlot+150 (37.1% beyond 151, 5.2% beyond 155, 0.0% beyond 160). This is not a rounding nuisance: the trailing fills are disproportionately LATE SELLS, and dropping one flips a wallet from closed to open, which shrinks fieldClosedRoundTrips — itself a gate at minFieldRoundTrips 10. So a too-narrow span silently changes gate outcomes. 160 covers 100% of observed windows with margin over the observed max of 158. STAGE 0 DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE THIS: it measures each committed launch over its own stored window, because the 1,502-pair reproduction against wallet_launch_pnl.csv is computed that way and that regression guard is not traded for cosmetic consistency between the two paths.
justification.seekMarginMs: The walk seeks from createdAtMs + windowMs + this, so a vendor mint time running EARLY by less than 5s cannot cut the tail off the window before the slot trim ever sees it. It replaces a tail-truncation detector that could not discriminate — launches simply stop trading before the nominal window end (p50 observed span 151 against a 160 span), so any such detector fires on nearly every launch and carries no information. Designing the failure out beats reporting it. COST: the walk still pages BACKWARDS to the mint and still trims by slot afterwards, so the margin only adds rows at the newest end — about 5s of trading, roughly 32 fills at the tape's p50 of 381 fills per 60s, i.e. at most one extra page of 100. maxRequestsPerLaunch is 18, about 13-14 successful pages at the measured shed rate against a measured p95 of 13 pages, so that page fits inside the existing cap and the 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 stage arithmetic is unchanged. THIS IS A CURSOR HINT AND NOT A TOLERANCE: the pre-mint tripwire still compares ts < createdAtMs with ZERO slack (the measured gap is exactly 0 on all 235 committed launches) and coverage is still discharged only by the endpoint explicitly saying nothing older exists.
justification.maxKeylessRequests: Stage 2's own sub-ceiling, enforced on its own client so it cannot eat the --consistency pass's budget. 3 x 8 x 18 = 432 is the exact declared worst case, so no plan-level truncation is possible: the ceiling and the plan agree, and the dry run prints both. Typical cost is far lower - at the measured p50 of 4 pages plus shedding it is about 6 requests a launch, so roughly 144 for a full run. At the pinned 7s pacing for this host that is about 17 minutes typical against about 50 minutes worst case, and the run prints both so an operator does not mistake a slow walk for a hang. A launch is only started when a full per-launch cap of headroom remains, so a run can never abandon a launch half-walked.
